content: 1. We assume that there is no mortality from cervical cancer in true negatives (TN) and false positives (FP). To estimate cervical cancer mortality, we assume 250 deaths occur per 350 women diagnosed with cervical cancer. 2. We assume that cervical cancer does not occur in TN or FP cases. The incidence of cervical cancer is based on an age-standardized rate in Eastern Africa, which is 350 cases per 100,000 women. Of these, 2% have CIN 2+ (20,000 women), with a subsequent 30% regression rate, leaving 14,000 women with persistent CIN 2+. 3. We assume that CIN 2+ does not occur in TN and FP cases. Our model calculations are based on a 70% natural persistence rate of CIN 2+ without treatment (30% regression) in false negatives (FN). The incidence and mortality of cervical cancer are subtracted from the CIN 2+ cases in FN. 4. We assume that major bleeding does not occur in TN and FN cases, as they are not treated. However, 0.001705 of the population treated with cold knife conization (CKC), based on pooled proportions from observational studies without independent controls, will experience major bleeding. 5. We assume a 5% population risk of premature delivery in 1% of women who become pregnant. Among those treated with CKC, 0.001705 of the population will experience premature delivery. 6. We did not identify any data regarding the risk of infertility following treatment for CIN 2+. 7. We assume that major infections do not occur in TN and FN cases, as they are not treated. However, 0.000888 of the population treated with CKC will experience major infections. 8. We assume that minor infections do not occur in TN and FN cases, as they are not treated. However, 0.009368 of the population treated with CKC will experience minor infections. 9. The number of cancers detected during first-time screening was calculated based on data from Sankaranarayanan et al. (2005). For single screening tests, the number of cancers was calculated as screen-detected cancers in women participating in the screening program. For tests involving colposcopy, the number was calculated as screen-detected plus clinically detected cancers. In cases where multiple tests were used (e.g., HPV test followed by VIA), the higher number of cancers detected between tests was used. No cancers would be detected in the no screen group. This calculation reflects the prevalence of cancer at the time of screening, not the annual incidence of cervical cancer. 10. The no screen group numbers were calculated using the same assumptions as for FN cases, except for premature delivery, which was based on the baseline risk in the population. It is assumed that the recurrence of CIN is constant across age groups, but the incidence of cervical cancer and associated mortality increases with age, reducing the overall recurrence of CIN (as a proportion of those with CIN will develop cancer or die). These data are intended for comparisons across screen-and-treat strategies, not within columns for different age groups.
